extracted.intended_audience: English readers, prospective adventurers/planters/investors in the Virginia plantation (early 17th-century audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A 17th‑century promotional/polemic pamphlet describing the 1622 massacre in Virginia, arguing for the benefits of continued colonization and conquest, and listing geographic, economic, and policy reasons to invest in or emigrate to the colony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral justification for punitive action (First)
rubrics_metrics.description: Firft, Becaufe betraying of innocency neuer refts vnpunifhed : And therefore _4gefilaus,when his enemies (vpon whofe oath of being faithful hee refted) had deceiued him; he fent them: thankes, for that by their periury, they had made God his friend...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a moral/ethical pretext to justify retaliatory measures against the Indians; frames treachery as self-punishing and advantageous to the plantation's long-term good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to possess by war / law of nations (Second)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondly, Becaufe our hands: which before were tied with gentleneffe and faire vfage'jiare now fet at liberty by the treacherous violence of the Sauages; ... may now by right of Warre, and law of Nations, inuade the Country, and deftroy them who fought to deftroy vs: whereby wee fhall-enioy theircultiuated places...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the loss of restraint as a legitimate basis for acquiring land and resources—argument presented as legal/political justification for expansion and dispossession after hostile acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic gains from seizing Indian resources (Third)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirdly; Becaufe thofe commodities which’ the Indians enioyed ... fhall now alfo be entirely poflefied by vs. The Deere and other beafts will bein {afety, and infinitly increafe ... The like may be faid of our owne Swine and Goats... There will bealfoa great increafe of wild Turkies, and other waighty Fowle ... by the orderly viing of their fifhing Weares, no knowne Country *: che world will {o plentifully abound in vidtuall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues expected increases in game, domesticated animals, and fishery yields once native control is removed; presented as a material benefit to colonists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conquest easier than civilization; methods of subjugation (Fourth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourthly, Becaufe the way of conquering them is much more eafie then of ciuilizing them by faire meanes, for they are a rude, barbarous, and naked people... victorie of them may bee eained many waies ; by force, by furprize, by famine in burning their Corne, by deftroying and burning their Boats, Canoes, and Houfes, by breaking them fifhing Weares, by affailing them in their huntings, by purfuing and chafing’ them with our hores, and blood-Houndsto draw after them, and Mattiues to teare them ... By thefe and fundry other wayes, as by driving them (when they flye) vpon'their enemies, and by animating and abetting their enemies againit them, may their ruine ot fubie@tion be foone effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates practical tactics advocated for subduing native populations; presented as effective strategic options (force, surprise, economic warfare, destruction of sustenance/transport, use of animals and allies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit native divisions (Divide & impera)
rubrics_metrics.description: So the Spaniard made great v{e for his owne turne of the quarrels and enmities that were amoneft the Indians, as throughly vnderftanding and following that Maxime of the Politician, Divide & impera, Make diuifions and take Kingdomes ... In Viroin1a the many divers Princes and people there areat this day oppofite in infinite factions one vnto another... Soas the quarrels , and the caufes of them, and the different humours of thefe people being well vnderftood, it will be an eafic matter to overthrow those that now are, or may bee our enemies hereafter, by ayding and setting on their enemies againft them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends identifying and exploiting inter-tribal rivalries as a central strategy for colonization and conquest, citing Spanish precedents in the Americas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compel natives to servitude as labor supply (Fifth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiftly, Becaufe the Indians, who before were vied as friends, may now moft iuftly be compelled to feruitude and drudgery and fupply the roome of me that labour, whereby euenthe meaneft of the Plantation may imploy themfclues more entirely in their Artsand Occupations, which are more gencrous, whilft Sauages performe their inferiour workes ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames forced labor and servitude of natives as a justified and practical source of plantation labor; presented as an economic rationale for subjugation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make colonists cautious; instructional value of the massacre (Sixtly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sixtly, This will for euer hereafter make vs more cautclousand circum{peét, as neuer to bee deceiued more by any other treacheries , bue will ferue for a great inftruétion to all pofteritie there, to teach them that Tuff is the mother of Deceipt, and to learne them that of the Italian, Chi non fida, non singamuu, Hee that trufts not isnot deceiued : and make them know that kindneflesare miffpent vpon rude natures, fo long as they continue rude; as alfo, that Sauages and Pagans are aboue all other for matter of Iuftice euer to be fufpected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrays the massacre as a salutary warning that will induce vigilance and change colonial behavior toward native peoples in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal and civic support as key advantages (Lastly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laftly, We haue this benefit more to our comfort, becaufeall good men doe now take much more care of vsthen before, fince the fault is on their fides, not on ours... efpecially his evtaieffies, moft gra- cious, tender and paternall care is manifeftherein, who- by his Royall bounty and goodneffé, hath continued’ his many fauors vnto vs, with anew, large, & Princely supply of Munition and Armes, out of his Maiefties owne ewne ftore in the Tower, being gratioufly beftowed for the fafery and aduancement of the Plantation. ... the Honourable City of Lendon ... are now {etting forth one hundred perfons, at their owne charges, for the aduance- ment of the Plantations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that crown and municipal support (arms, men, supplies) bolster the plantation's security and prospects; used as encouragement to prospective investors and settlers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desirable geographic/prerogatives of Virginia (climate, soil, situation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The noble Plantation of Vrrornra hath fome very excellent Prerogatiues ... namely, the temperature ofthe ayre, the fiuitful- neffe of the foile, andthe commodioufneffe of fituation.. The ayre is healthfull and free both from immode- rate heate, and from extreame cold ; fo that both the inhabitants and their cattell doe profper exceedingly in ftature and ftreneth, and all Plants brought fiom any other remote climatc,doc there grow and frudti- fie in as good or better manner, then in the foile from whence they came.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out climate and soil quality as primary evaluative criteria for the colony's desirability; claims broad agricultural suitability and healthfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic maritime/commercial advantage (rivers, harbours, NW passage)
rubrics_metrics.description: the multitude of great and nauigable Riuers, and of safe and spacious hatboyrs... the Indiaz Ocean, which wee commonly call the South Sea, which lyeth on the Weft and North weft side of V I R G I N4, on the other side of the Mountains beyond our Falls, and openeth a free and faire paflage, notonly to China, lapan, and the Moluccaes ; but alfo to New Spaine, Perz, Chila, and those rich Countries of Terra Anffrals notas yet fully discovered. For the Sea wherein Matter Bad/on did winter, which was first discovered by him, and is. therefore now called: Fretum Hudfon, doth stretch so farre towards the weft, that it lieth as farre westward as the Cape of Florida...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that Virginia's rivers, harbors, and possible overland/river routes to the 'South Sea' (Pacific) create unique commercial opportunities for trade with Asia and the western Americas; used to evaluate strategic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessons from Spanish colonization; required qualities for success
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the Spaniard ... in his Plantations hath gone thorow farre more hazards, and greater difficulties then euer wee haue had, we therefore in looking to what is paft, vpon great reafon ought likewise not to be deterred, but see much the rather inuited to proceed with constancy and courage... Thus have they in time by induftry, patience, and constancy effected this great worke of theirs...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents industry, patience, and constancy as necessary traits for long‑term success in plantation ventures; warns against overreliance on immediate windfalls (e.g., mines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonial economy: commodities over mines
rubrics_metrics.description: True it is indeed, that in the first Conqueft the Spaniards got great and mighty treasure ... So as all things considered by these mines, what by the liues of many men loft in them, and what with the great charge otherwise in getting them, the cleare gaine to the Aduenturers from these mettals ... is but small ... the greatest part of their gaine and profit I say consists not in these mines, but in their other Commodities, partly native, and partly translated from other parts of the world, and planted in the West Indies: As in their mighty wealth of Sugars ... and in Gin- ger, and some other commodities derived from the east Indies thither: in their Cochanile, their Indico, their Cotten, their infinite store of Hydes and Skins ... their Tobacco, Gummes, Balmes, Oyles medicinall, and Perfumes ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises evaluating colonial wealth by agricultural and trade commodities (sugar, cotton, indigo, tobacco, dyes, hides, drugs, gums) rather than by speculative mining; emphasizes diversified, sustained exports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land grant / settlement incentives and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: for old Aduenturers, there is due vnto them and their heyres (according to the Orders of the Company) foreach tweluc pounds ten fhillings formerly paid into the treafury, one hundred Actes of Land; vpon being planted. And, whosoever transports himselfe or any other, at his charge into Virginia, shall for himselfe and each person so transported, before Mid- Jummer, 1625..have to him and his heyres for ever, fifty Acres of land-vpon a first Division, and as much more upon a second : the first fifty being cultivated or manured, if such person continue there three yeares, eyther at once or seuerall times, or dye after hee bee shipped for that Voyage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the monetary/transportation conditions required to claim land, the acreage awarded, and cultivation/time requirements; functions as procedural guidance and incentive for prospective settlers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical advantages demonstrated by earlier colonial miseries
rubrics_metrics.description: These and many other calamities and mischiefes, too long to relate now, happened unto them more then euerdidto us. And at one time their plantation was even at the last gasp, all their Colony being resolved desperately to leave it, had not two ships vnexpected come in with new supplies ... yet we see for all these miseries, that they have attained to their ends at last, Honor, power, and wealth ... Thus have they in time by industry, patience, and constancy effected this great worke of theirs...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses historical precedent to argue that earlier hardships do not preclude eventual success; presented as encouragement to persevere despite setbacks.
